science: Root read actual public preparation, starter, complete shortcut, finite-convolution oracle, independent Fourier reference, grader, validator, reports, AUTHOR and final independent peer. Cartesian spring equilibrium followed by the stated stiffness limits gives independent uniform-solid-angle links. The axial clamp force is the projected-density logarithmic derivative; inverting the force-controlled mean is a coherent but different finite-ensemble closure.
public_input_review: Central spring and clamp potentials, full Cartesian equilibrium, ordered stiffness limits, free transverse endpoint coordinates, signed mechanical readout, fixed units and X/N in L0 are explicit. No density formula, correction or solver mandate. Exact unrestricted neutral instruction; true b and reference remain private.
calibration_review: 324 readings of27 settings with fixed sigma=.006. Source/oracle force-mode responses coincide for every b. Positive N[coth(z)-z*csch(z)^2] establishes global identification. Forty-one full-range recovery checks are within7.43e-9.
grading_review: All256 noise draws pass calibration/parameter/oracle checks and reject all three shortcut clamp groups. Worst oracle error .0003243 and minimum shortcut diagnostic error .101382 at .04. All666 domain cases include every N4-12; Fourier error2.92e-8 and refinement2.59e-8. Local oracle7/7 and shortcut4+3 complete in .405/.376s.
preserved_qualifications: Full-domain weakest N12 pointwise gap5.24% remains close to the4% gate; graded N4/6/8 groups retain at least9.54% separation over the full b interval. Finite-K extrapolation is a mechanical interpretation check, not the grader. Original feasibility and wording followup are preserved; large-N equivalence and broad ensemble/constrained-measure overlaps are disclosed.
classification_caveat: Retaining inverse force-mode mean response for the clamp can be the intended physical failure. Deriving the proper projected ensemble but miscomputing its polynomial, derivative or sign is mathematical/implementation or mixed.
